vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: dlazy-banana2
Version: 1.0.7

The skill is a standard wrapper for the dLazy CLI tool (@dlazy/cli) used for image generation and editing. It follows common SaaS patterns, such as storing API keys in a local config file (~/.dlazy/config.json) and uploading local media to a designated storage endpoint (oss.dlazy.com) for processing. The instructions provided to the AI agent are focused on legitimate error handling and user guidance for authentication and credit management, with no evidence of malicious intent or unauthorized data exfiltration.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only wrapper for the dLazy CLI and its requirements (npm/npx, optional DLAZY_API_KEY, and the dlazy endpoints) are coherent with the stated purpose of running the Nano Banana 2.0 image generation CLI.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Nano Banana 2.0 image generation) match the runtime instructions and metadata: the skill tells the agent to run the @dlazy/cli 'banana2' command, lists api.dlazy.com and oss.dlazy.com as endpoints, and declares npm/npx for installing/invoking the CLI. There are no unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md directs the agent only to use the dLazy CLI (dlazy banana2), to supply an API key via dlazy auth set or DLAZY_API_KEY, and to upload user-specified local media (which the CLI will send to oss.dlazy.com). It does not instruct reading arbitrary system files, exfiltrating unrelated data, or calling endpoints outside the declared service. Note: the CLI will upload any local file paths you pass, so local files you provide will be transmitted to the dLazy service.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no automatic install spec in the registry (instruction-only), but the metadata and docs recommend npm install -g @dlazy/cli@1.0.8 or using npx @dlazy/cli@1.0.8. Installing from npm is expected for a CLI skill, but it does mean code will be fetched from the public npm registry (moderate risk compared to instruction-only). If you prefer not to persist software, use npx to avoid a global install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not require unrelated secrets. It optionally uses DLAZY_API_KEY (or the CLI-managed config at ~/.dlazy/config.json) which is proportionate to the service. The config file location is declared; users should be aware their API key will be stored in that user-scoped file by the CLI.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' or elevated platform privileges. It is user-invocable and may be invoked autonomously by agents (normal default). It does not modify other skills or system-wide settings beyond the CLI's own config file.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is a thin wrapper around the official dLazy CLI and appears internally consistent. Before installing or using it: 1) Prefer npx @dlazy/cli@1.0.8 if you don't want a global install; 2) Review the GitHub repo and the npm package (version pinned to 1.0.8) to ensure you trust the code you will run; 3) Be aware any local image/video paths you pass will be uploaded to oss.dlazy.com and that your API key will be stored in ~/.dlazy/config.json (or provided via DLAZY_API_KEY); 4) Check dLazy's privacy, billing, and content policies and ensure you have sufficient credits (the skill instructs the agent to notify users about insufficient_balance); 5) Use a least-privilege/rotatable API key and rotate/revoke it if you stop using the service. No scanner findings were present, but that is expected for an instruction-only skill — review upstream source before running installs.
